body: Vale of White Horse District Council
summary: Motion on Cearn (proposed by Cllr Lee Evans) passed with amendments. As amended: solar should go on non-agricultural land first and avoid high-grade farmland; local shared ownership or benefit schemes and biodiversity gain; the Vale should not bear NSIP harms while benefits leave the district; cumulative impact with Botley West, the West Oxfordshire Energy Park and the reservoir must be considered. Resolves: Cabinet to develop a renewable energy policy and engage the developer on community benefits; Leader to write to the Defra Secretary of State and the OCC Cabinet Member for Transport. Vote and final wording await the minutes
note: The motion asks for a letter to Defra, but the decision-maker for Cearn is the DESNZ Secretary of State

body: Vale of White Horse District Council
summary: Written answers: Cearn is decided by the Secretary of State; the council is working with the Oxfordshire Association of Local Councils so parishes can input; officers are taking a programme-wide approach to cumulative impacts through the Joint Local Plan
No Cabinet decision, highways response or motion on Cearn found
note: Watch for the scoping response from OCC as highways and flood authority

summary: Monitoring Cearn and attended initial events; no formal position yet. Its 2023 position paper wants Grades 1, 2 and 3a land avoided, rooftops and brownfield first, and treats cumulative impact as critical
